clips.text_zh: 又見到人問買Cybercab放落Robotaxi network收錢⋯⋯買車都要諗埋俾Tesla抽佣，我哋呢啲prop firm 廢柴真係輸到唔敢再諗。靠AI續命，遲啲連車都唔需要司機啦 🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Redpill me on buying Cybercabs and putting them to work on the Tesla Robotaxi network for passive income. Has anyone actually run the numbers on daily earnings after Tesla takes its cut, insurance, charging, and maintenance? Or is this just another hopium thread for bagholders who missed TSLA at $200?
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread asking whether buying a Cybercab for the Tesla Robotaxi network is realistic passive income.

signal.rationale: OP implies long-term Robotaxi optimism on TSLA, but the framing is hopium, not a clean setup.

clips.text_en_b2: I keep seeing people ask about buying Cybercabs and dropping them onto Tesla's Robotaxi network to generate passive income. Has anyone actually crunched the numbers on daily earnings after Tesla skims its cut, insurance, charging, and maintenance? Or is this yet another hopium fantasy for bagholders who got in late on TSLA? Because once you factor in depreciation and idle downtime, the margins look razor-thin at best, and the whole proposition smells like cope dressed up as a business plan.
clips.text_en_c1: I keep seeing posts hyping Cybercabs as a hands-off revenue stream once they are deployed on Tesla's Robotaxi network. Before anyone commits capital, has anyone genuinely modelled the actual daily yields, factoring in Tesla's platform commission, depreciation, charging costs, insurance premiums, and routine maintenance? Or is this simply another exercise in hopium aimed at bagholders who regret not loading up on TSLA back when it traded under two hundred dollars? For those of us bleeding out in prop firm evaluations, the prospect of yet another leveraged punt feels less like passive income and more like an elaborate exit liquidity arrangement waiting to happen.
clips.text_en_c2: I would appreciate a rigorous, dispassionate breakdown of the economics underpinning the proposition that one ought to purchase a Tesla Cybercab and deploy it within the company's nascent Robotaxi network as a vehicle for generating semi-passive income. Has anyone genuinely modelled the daily yield net of Tesla's platform commission, insurance premiums, depreciation, scheduled maintenance, and the residual cost of charging? Or is this thread merely the latest exercise in collective self-delusion, a refuge for those who arrived late to TSLA at fifty or two hundred dollars and now clutch at whatever narrative might vindicate the position? I remain, as ever, sceptical to the point of paralysis, given how thoroughly prior ventures have stripped me of both capital and conviction.

clips.text_zh: Bitcoin定黃金揸十年？BTC成日pump完又chop，黄金慢但至少唔會歸零。我prop firm 帳戶又輸緊，兩樣都冇錢加倉，真係廢物 🧐
clips.text_en_b1: Bitcoin vs Gold. If you had to hold only one for the next 10 years, would you choose Bitcoin or gold? What makes your choice better than the other? Gold is slow and boring, but BTC gives you 70% drawdowns every bear cycle and then prints new highs. Which actually wins over a decade?
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread debating Bitcoin versus gold as a ten-year hold.

signal.rationale: OP is implicitly asking which is the better long-term store of value; framing favors BTC upside over a decade.

clips.text_en_b2: Bitcoin versus gold: if you had to pick one and hold it for the next ten years, which would you choose? Gold creeps up slowly while BTC pumps hard then chops sideways, delivering brutal 70% drawdowns every bear cycle before printing fresh highs. The boring case for gold is that it never goes to zero, whereas Bitcoin's upside comes with serious tail risk. Over a full decade, which asset actually comes out ahead once you factor in volatility and real returns?
clips.text_en_c1: If you were compelled to hold a single asset for the coming decade, would you anchor your portfolio to Bitcoin or to gold? Bitcoin undeniably delivers spectacular bull runs, yet each cycle has historically prefaced a seventy percent drawdown before printing fresh highs, which makes the volatility difficult to stomach. Gold, by contrast, drifts glacially and rarely excites, but it has never gone to zero across several millennia of recorded price action. Over a ten-year horizon, which genuinely compounds wealth more reliably? My prop firm account is bleeding again, so I cannot afford to add to either position, yet the question continues to nag.
clips.text_en_c2: Forced to hold a single asset over the ensuing decade, does one rationally elect Bitcoin or gold, and on what principled basis? Gold, for all its plodding tedium, has the consoling virtue of never having liquidated its holders to zero, whereas Bitcoin, notwithstanding its capacity to print successive all-time highs, subjects its devotees to drawdowns of sixty or seventy percent with metronomic regularity before the next leg higher commences. Which, then, is the superior ten-year store of value once one accounts for volatility, liquidity premia, and the gravitational pull of reflexive speculation? I, regrettably, possess neither asset in any meaningful quantity, my proprietary trading account having once again depleted what little margin I had earmarked for accumulation.

clips.text_zh: CloseAI 出 Astra 又話係AGI⋯⋯我份surveying工遲早俾AI搶，連HKIE考牌都仲未過，廢。AI取代白領再殺到藍領，我哋呢啲工程仔最慘 lol
clips.text_en_b1: CloseAI's new Astra model. They claim it is AGI. So... what's your verdict, /g/? Is this actually AGI or just another chatbot with better marketing? Can it replace a junior engineer yet, or is it still hallucinating code that does not compile?
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread reacting to CloseAI claiming its new Astra model is AGI.

signal.rationale: Tech/AI culture thread, not a trade setup.

clips.text_en_b2: CloseAI just dropped Astra and they're claiming it's AGI again. So what's the verdict, /g/? Is this genuinely artificial general intelligence or merely another chatbot wrapped in slicker marketing? It still hallucinates code that fails to compile half the time, so I doubt it can replace a junior engineer just yet. Although progress keeps compounding, the gap between demo footage and reliable white-collar work remains wider than the hype suggests.
clips.text_en_c1: CloseAI has unveiled their latest model, branded Astra, and unsurprisingly the marketing materials once again proclaim it as a meaningful step toward AGI. So what is the verdict from /g/? Is this genuinely a qualitative leap, or merely another autoregressive chatbot wrapped in slicker rhetoric? The benchmarks look formidable on paper, but can it actually replace a junior software engineer, or does it still hallucinate entire functions that refuse to compile when subjected to scrutiny? For those of us clinging to mid-tier technical roles, each such announcement feels less like progress and more like an obituary written in advance.
clips.text_en_c2: CloseAI has unveiled Astra, and predictably, the marketing apparatus has once again anointed it AGI, a designation that has now become so thoroughly debased as to signify little beyond capital-raising intent. Is this genuinely the threshold of general intelligence, or is it merely a more eloquent chatbot draped in the customary veneer of benchmark theatre? I remain unconvinced, particularly as my own modest surveying practice faces an existential encroachment from precisely these systems, and the professional examination I have yet to pass seems an increasingly quaint credential. The trajectory is unmistakable: erstwhile white-collar bastions erode first, followed inexorably by the trades, and we middling engineers shall, I suspect, be consumed somewhere in the unhappy middle.

clips.text_zh: 印尼Krakatoa又爆，今次係大爆發。東南亞啲火山灰飄到香港都未定，出trip都唔方便，我OT搞埋HKIE筆記好煩 🙏
clips.text_en_b1: HAPPENING NOW: MAJOR ERUPTION AT THE KRAKATOA VOLCANO IN INDONESIA. BNO Desk just posted the alert with the ash plume visible from satellite. Is anyone tracking flight cancellations into Hong Kong yet, or is the wind pushing the ash away from us this time?
clips.source_hint: /pol/ thread sharing breaking news of a major Krakatoa eruption.

signal.rationale: Breaking disaster news thread, no trade implied.

clips.text_en_b2: BREAKING: a major eruption is underway at Krakatoa in Indonesia, with the ash plume clearly captured on satellite imagery by BNO Desk. Is anyone tracking flight cancellations into Hong Kong yet, or is the prevailing wind pushing the ash cloud away from us this time? Because depending on the jet stream, even a relatively small eruption can ground regional flights for days, and I'd rather not get stuck at the airport again.
clips.text_en_c1: DEVELOPING: A significant eruption has been recorded at Krakatoa in Indonesia, with the BNO Desk confirming satellite imagery of a substantial ash plume rising from the caldera. Given the prevailing wind patterns across the South China Sea, is anyone monitoring whether flight routes into Hong Kong International are likely to be disrupted in the coming days, or is the ash trajectory projected to bypass us entirely? Previous eruptions have grounded regional carriers for forty-eight hours or more, and any cancellation cascade would compound the chaos for travellers already navigating reduced schedules. Stay safe and keep your itineraries flexible.
clips.text_en_c2: BREAKING: a substantial eruptive event is presently unfolding at Krakatoa, Indonesia, with the BNO Desk disseminating satellite imagery of an ash column of considerable vertical extent. The pertinent question, particularly for those of us with imminent regional commitments, is whether prevailing stratospheric winds will propagate the ejecta northeastward toward the Hong Kong flight corridor or deflect it harmlessly over open ocean. Disruption to inbound and outbound schedules, while not yet formally announced, would scarcely be unprecedented given the volcano's recent cadence. I am presently engaged in overtime obligations and the interminable preparation required for an HKIE examination, neither of which is materially improved by the prospect of an unscheduled grounding at Chek Lap Kok.

clips.text_zh: Fallout 4 係咪真係好game？當年好似好趕release。LOL S15打完等緊下一場，轉下game都ok 👍
clips.text_en_b1: Is Fallout 4 really as good as people say it is? When I first played it, it felt like a game that was developed too quickly and rushed to release. The map feels empty in some areas and the dialogue system is worse than Fallout 3 or New Vegas. Is the mod scene the only reason it still has a following?
clips.source_hint: /v/ thread debating whether Fallout 4 was rushed at launch.

signal.rationale: Gaming opinion thread, no market signal.

clips.text_en_b2: Is Fallout 4 genuinely as good as the fanbase claims, or was it rushed out the door to meet a deadline? When I played it initially, certain zones felt empty and the dialogue system was a clear downgrade from Fallout 3 and New Vegas. The quest design also leans heavily on radiant filler. While the modding community has kept the game alive for years, I'd argue the core experience didn't quite live up to the hype at launch.
clips.text_en_c1: Is Fallout 4 genuinely deserving of the acclaim it continues to receive, or has nostalgia inflated its reputation beyond recognition? Upon revisiting it recently, I was struck by how evidently the title was rushed toward release, with several zones feeling conspicuously underbaked and the dialogue wheel representing a regression from the branching depth that characterised Fallout 3 and New Vegas. That said, the modding community has effectively remastered the experience over the past ten years, which arguably accounts for the bulk of its enduring appeal. Is the sustained player base essentially a testament to modders rather than to Bethesda's original design vision?
clips.text_en_c2: I find myself returning, with some ambivalence, to the question of whether Fallout 4 merits its canonical standing or whether that reputation is largely a function of brand inertia and modder industriousness. On a fresh playthrough, one perceives the unmistakable fingerprints of a truncated development cycle: certain regions feel conspicuously underserved, the procedural density of New Vegas is conspicuously absent, and the dialoguewheel, however serviceable, represents a retrograde step relative to its predecessors. That the title retains a fervent following is, I suspect, attributable less to its intrinsic design than to the staggering volume of community-authored content. The League of Legends season being concluded, I have resorted to this title as a palliative until fixtures resume.

clips.text_zh: OHP就嚟1pl8，bench仲未到2pl8，squat同deadlift更加廢。肥仔信今日又叫我夾gym，我話我prop firm 輸緊錢冇心情lol
clips.text_en_b1: 1/2/3/4. I am closer to a 1-plate overhead press than I am to a 2-plate bench, 3-plate squat, or 4-plate deadlift. I think I will have a 1-pl8 OHP for reps in about a month or two if I keep adding 2.5kg per week. Press is lagging but bench is lagging even harder.

signal.rationale: Lifting progress post, no trade setup.

clips.text_en_b2: My lifts are all over the place: I'm closing in on a one-plate overhead press, yet my bench is still miles away from two plates, and my squat and deadlift are even more embarrassing. If I keep adding 2.5 kilos per week, I should hit a solid one-pl8 OHP for reps within a month or two. Although my press is lagging, my bench is lagging considerably harder, and I'm not sure which weak point to address first.
clips.text_en_c1: My strength totals are approaching the fabled one-two-three-four milestone, yet the distribution is frankly embarrassing. I should realistically hit a one-plate overhead press for clean reps within six to eight weeks if I continue adding the standard two and a half kilograms weekly, provided my recovery holds up. My bench, however, remains stubbornly anchored below two plates, while my squat and deadlift lag so far behind that they scarcely warrant discussion at this point. A training partner invited me to grind sets today, but honestly, watching my prop firm account bleed has rather sapped my enthusiasm for voluntary suffering.
clips.text_en_c2: I find myself, with characteristic frustration, considerably closer to a one-plate overhead press than to a two-plate bench, a three-plate squat, or a four-plate deadlift, the latter two remaining frankly embarrassing. On the press, provided I continue my programme of weekly two-and-a-half-kilogram increments, a single-rep one-plate milestone ought to materialise within the ensuing fortnight or so; the bench, however, lags to a degree that defies any comfortable narrative explanation. My training partner, irrepressibly, has again summoned me to the gym, and I have declined on the grounds that my proprietary trading account, once more in the red, has rather comprehensively extinguished whatever residual enthusiasm I might otherwise have mustered.

clips.text_zh: 鏈鋸人volume 6同7好正，我冇睇Reze arc戲院版，但睇返manga幾enjoy。動畫season 1雖然俾人話，但鏡頭幾cinema。Gundam 00之後又多套追 lol
clips.text_en_b1: Chainsaw Man volume 6 and 7. I didn't watch the Reze arc movie when it was out in theaters, but I always liked season 1 so I recently started reading the manga. I can see why everyone loves the movie. The manga is very enjoyable. The cinematic panel layouts fit the direction season 1 went for.
clips.source_hint: /a/ thread about the Chainsaw Man manga and the Reze arc movie.

signal.rationale: Anime recommendation thread, no market signal.

clips.text_en_b2: I finally got around to reading Chainsaw Man volumes 6 and 7, and honestly they hit different on the page. I skipped the Reze arc theatrical release, but since I enjoyed season 1, I figured the manga would be worth picking up. The cinematic panel layouts really do echo the visual direction the anime went for, so I get why fans fell in love with the movie. Looks like I've got another series to binge after Gundam 00.
clips.text_en_c1: Chainsaw Man volumes six and seven are an absolute revelation on the page, particularly once the Reze arc unfolds in its full unfiltered glory. I regrettably skipped the theatrical release when it was screening locally, but revisiting the source chapters has been thoroughly rewarding, and I finally comprehend why audiences responded so enthusiastically to the cinematic adaptation. The manga's panel compositions are genuinely inventive, employing widescreen layouts that feel almost storyboarded, which directly mirrors the visual ambition that the inaugural season pursued so distinctively. With Gundam 00 concluded, this is precisely the kind of auteur-driven follow-up that justifies a subscription.
clips.text_en_c2: Chainsaw Man volumes six and seven constitute, in my estimation, the work's creative apex, the Reze arc translating to the printed page with an intensity that evidently justified the recent cinematic release, which I regrettably neglected to attend during its theatrical run. Having only belatedly commenced the manga, I find myself persuaded of the widespread enthusiasm: the panel compositions are uncommonly cinematic, and the visual syntax dovetails seamlessly with the directorial register that the inaugural season so memorably established. It is, I think, the rare adaptation wherein the source material and the animated rendering mutually reinforce one another. With Gundam 00 concluded, I now possess yet another series to occupy whatever slender leisure my schedule permits.
